description:
## Finding

`ChatBackend::apply_space_patch`'s rustdoc
(`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:441-509`) does not state
the post-mutation invariant on `Space.memberCount`.

The space.rs handler at `src/space.rs:766` documents the
*inbound* rejection rule:

```
/// - `id`, `createdAt`, `memberCount` are server-set and rejected in updates.
```

That covers "client cannot write memberCount". It does NOT cover
"backend must recompute memberCount after every AddMember /
RemoveMember op so the served Space.memberCount equals the
post-mutation `members.len()`".

The integration test asserts the post-mutation invariant:

`crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/role_member_apply.rs:951-954`:

```rust
assert_eq!(
    get_resp["list"][0]["memberCount"], 1,
    "memberCount tracks members.len()"
);
```

## What goes wrong for a third-party implementer

A backend that:
1. Persists `Space.memberCount` as a stored field at create time, AND
2. Persists the members list as a separate aggregate, AND
3. Updates the members list on AddMember / RemoveMember but
   forgets to recompute and rewrite the stored `memberCount`,

ships a working `Space/get` (returns the stored value), a working
`Space/set` AddMember (members aggregate updates), and a quietly
inconsistent wire output where `memberCount: 5` is served while
`members` has 8 entries — drift silently grows with every
mutation.

The natural minimal implementation is to store memberCount once
and trust it. The natural correct implementation is to compute
memberCount from members at every read OR recompute and rewrite
it after every mutation. The doc does not say which.

## Recommendation

Add one sentence to `apply_space_patch`'s rustdoc:

> Server-set fields on the target Space (`memberCount`,
> `updatedAt`, etc.) MUST be kept consistent with the post-
> mutation state. Backends MAY store these as cached values
> that they recompute on every mutation, or MAY compute them
> lazily at read time; either is acceptable as long as
> `Space/get` returns values consistent with `Space/get`'s
> `members` array.

## Engineering basis

- Test assertion at `role_member_apply.rs:951-954` verbatim.
- Handler doc at `src/space.rs:766` documents only the inbound
  side.
- Rustdoc at `backend.rs:441-509` end-to-end: no mention of
  `memberCount`.

## Priority justification

P3 because:
- The invariant is "obvious in retrospect" for any implementer
  who thinks carefully about cached-vs-derived fields.
- The kit's tests catch the divergence if a third-party backend
  plugs into them.
- Failure mode is wire-level inconsistency that monitoring
  clients (count-based UI badges) will surface visually
  quickly.

Not P2 because the bug shape is recoverable (a fresh `Space/get`
+ recompute fixes the drift) and the contract is widely
understood as "cached aggregates need refresh".

Not opinion because a third-party implementer can and will get
this wrong on a first pass — the natural-minimal-implementation
trap is real.
title: API contract: apply_space_patch rustdoc does not state Space.memberCount must track members.len() post-mutation
